title: ContextVM and canonical Nostr runtime migration

intended_behavior.mutations: Production web, CLI, MCP, and backend control-plane mutation paths use ContextVM JSON-RPC 2.0 over Nostr kind 25910, normally wrapped with CEP-4/NIP-59 random-key gift-wrap kinds 1059 or 21059 where encrypted transport is available.
intended_behavior.reads: Production clients read canonical observable/state, audit, status, discovery, and relay topology kinds: 30900, 4903, 30315, 11316-11320, 30002, 30078, and applicable standard NIPs.
intended_behavior.legacy_runtime: Legacy Bahia custom request/status/result/read-model/encrypted kinds are not production reactor/subscriber/client runtime support outside startup migration, historical conversion, and fail-closed fixtures.
intended_behavior.deletions: Deletions use NIP-09 kind 5 where relay-level Nostr deletion semantics apply; domain projections may also publish canonical tombstone replacements when durable state semantics require them.
intended_behavior.documentation: User-facing docs identify final ContextVM transport, canonical observable kinds, NIP-09 deletion behavior, and migration-only legacy boundaries.
intended_behavior.encrypted_results: Browser encrypted ContextVM result waiting terminates from correlated result EVENTs, explicit relay CLOSED/AUTH lifecycle failures, publish failure cleanup, or caller-provided operation cancellation; it does not use timeout-based completion semantics.

out_of_scope: Relay operator policy changes outside Bahia runtime/docs
Additional product features beyond the Nostr-native ContextVM migration

completed_streams.result: CEP-4/NIP-59 random-key gift-wrap support for 1059/21059 around inner ContextVM 25910 implemented in encrypted transport.
Production runtime legacy kind reactor/subscriber support removed; legacy kinds isolated to startup migration/fixtures.
Web/CLI client cutover to ContextVM/canonical observables completed.
Docs and PSTF artifacts finalized for the completed migration.
Docs/PSTF pass rewrote target production documentation to describe ContextVM 25910/CEP-4 and canonical observables, with old Bahia kind ranges marked historical/migration-only.

Browser encrypted ContextVM result waiting no longer uses timeout-based terminal semantics; deterministic unit tests inject result EVENT, EOSE, CLOSED/AUTH, publish failure, and AbortSignal cancellation paths.
